response.message:
your list is already stacked for tokyo, light for osaka, and nothing saved for [kyoto](kebi://area/jp/kyoto) yet, so kyoto is where i'll do the most work. here's how i'd shape the whole route, stop by stop.

---

kyoto (nothing saved here, so this one's on me)

since your saves lean heavily TikTok, i'll lead with the places that actually earn their visual reputation.

[Fushimi Inari Taisha](kebi://venue/798aea34-b234-4a06-b628-8d791d2396bf) is the one to anchor around, thousands of vermillion torii gates winding up the mountain. go at 7am before the tour groups arrive, because by 10am the lower section is elbow-to-elbow. the higher you climb, the quieter it gets. free, and worth every early alarm.

[Arashiyama Bamboo Forest](kebi://venue/f4b47463-0468-4adb-95a6-71f8a4b65393) has the same rule: morning is the move. the light through the bamboo in the early hours is the version you've seen on TikTok. pair it with the riverside area nearby and it's a calm half-day on its own.

[Kiyomizu-dera](kebi://venue/f8d8b1da-95bf-49fc-ade3-8433f3424185) is the hillside temple with the famous wooden stage jutting out over the valley. photogenic from every angle, and the walk up through the old Higashiyama lanes is half the experience. late afternoon light is the best slot.

[Nanzen-ji](kebi://venue/ae623fd4-0166-4741-9212-53b2b5d67e6c) is a quieter pick, a sprawling temple complex with a giant aqueduct running through it, one of those spots that genuinely surprises you. and [Philosopher's Path](kebi://venue/a2ba75fb-d758-4c11-a58a-12ff92281b79) is a canal-side walk connecting several temples, good for a slow hour between stops.

---

kyoto to osaka

only about 15 minutes by shinkansen, or 30 by regular express. easy leg, no stress.

---

osaka (nothing saved here either)

[Dotonbori](kebi://venue/1b247b82-0663-4f4f-be22-875f5ccc0a9f) is the anchor, the canal strip, the giant signs, the takoyaki and ramen stalls. best at night when everything's lit up. go hungry.

[Kuromon Market](kebi://venue/e35b0bea-bc55-4afb-adb5-a9cb8391e1b1) is your daytime food move, a covered market with fresh seafood and plenty to eat on the spot. morning or lunchtime is when it's at its best.

[Osaka Castle](kebi://venue/15a9d47a-0fb6-44ec-89ac-e7fb01492588) is worth a few hours, especially the grounds and the park around it.

you've got [Universal Studios Japan](kebi://venue/e68f1787-c5f6-4ed6-81b1-e0296a02ecf9) saved, that's a full day, so plan it as its own day rather than squeezing it around other things.

---

osaka to tokyo

the shinkansen from Shin-Osaka is about 2.5 hours on the Nozomi. one of the best train rides in the world, genuinely.

if you want to break the journey, [Mount Fuji](kebi://venue/67543868-5745-45bd-a5e9-4ab948480e30) is yours from your saves, it sits between Osaka and Tokyo and is worth a stop if you have a spare day. the most common base is Kawaguchiko on the north side, and the views from the fifth station are what most people go for. if you're going in August, the climbing season is open, so you could do the full hike, but it's a serious overnight effort. worth knowing it's a detour off the shinkansen line, so you'd need to factor in the extra transit.

---

tokyo (your list is stacked here)

[teamLab Planets](kebi://venue/3546d397-b212-4cb4-866a-3a87cd06c485) is yours from your saves, book this well ahead, it sells out fast. immersive digital art, water rooms, mirror installations. give it a couple of hours and don't wear clothes you mind getting wet at the ankles.

you've also saved [teamLab Borderless](kebi://venue/ce8d6832-b63e-4b15-8d39-50133dabbe62) (the Mori Building one). it's a different experience from Planets, more labyrinthine and exploratory, but since you've saved both, i'd pick one unless you have a genuinely spare day. Planets is the tighter, more intense experience; Borderless is the wander. if you only do one, Planets edges it.

[Shibuya Sky](kebi://venue/1bd47f5c-8855-4ba9-98e6-d4c6ccf6427f) is on your list, the rooftop above Shibuya Scramble. the sunset slot is the one to book, city in every direction and Fuji on a clear day.

[Shinjuku Gyoen](kebi://venue/1cf8682b-9ba4-4cc1-8a07-651c8b8b7b37) is yours too, a big national garden, great for a slow morning when you need to decompress from the city pace. pair it with [Meiji Jingu](kebi://venue/d4104468-7ac7-4674-8b91-a9b1b559fcfb), which is also on your list, a forested shrine a short walk away. those two together make a calm half-day rather than two separate trips.

[The Making of Harry Potter](kebi://venue/3d3d35f0-b134-4c2b-9dc0-e34ecef0576e) is saved as well, it's out in Toshimaen and is a solid half-day, but plan it as a standalone day since it's a separate trip from central Tokyo.
